title: ब्राजिलमा वामपन्थीको जित दक्षिणपन्थीलाई अश्वीकार, ट्रम्पका सहयोगी उम्मेदवारले कानूनी चुनौति दिने
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । ब्राजिलका राष्ट्रपति लुइज इनासियो लुला दा सिल्भा ऐतिहासिक चौथो कार्यकालका लागि पुनः निर्वाचित भएका छन् । तर, उनका प्रतिद्वन्द्वी तथा अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पका सहयोगी सिनेटर फ्लाभियो बोल्सोनारोले चुनावी नतिजा अस्वीकार गर्दै त्यसलाई कानुनी रूपमा चुनौती दिने बताएका छन् । ८० वर्षीय वामपन्थी नेता लुलाले दोस्रो चरणको निर्वाचनमा ५१ प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी मत प्राप्त गर्दै विजय हासिल गरेका छन् । उनको जित ल्याटिन अमेरिकाका विभिन्न देशमा दक्षिणपन्थी राजनीतिक धार बलियो बन्दै गइरहेका बेला वामपन्थीहरुका लागि राहत हो । लुलाभन्दा करिब ४४ लाख मतले पछाडि परेका बोल्सोनारोले सर्वोच्च अदालतले मतदानको समय अन्तिम समयमा दुई घण्टा थप्ने निर्णय गरेपछि नतिजामाथि प्रश्न उठाएका छन् । राजधानी ब्रासिलियामा समर्थकहरूलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उनले भने–घटनाक्रम जसरी अघि बढ्यो, त्यसलाई हेर्दा चुनावी नतिजा स्वीकार गर्न असम्भव छ । हामी कानुनी कदम चाल्नेछौँ, यो चुनाव रद्द गर्न माग गर्नेछौँ।” सन् १९८९ मा प्रत्यक्ष राष्ट्रपति निर्वाचनसुरु भएयता पहिलो चरणमा दोस्रो स्थानमा रहेका उम्मेदवारले दोस्रो चरणको मतदानपछि राष्ट्रपति पद जितेको यो पहिलो घटना भएको समाचारमा उल्लेख छ । लुलाको जितको प्रभाव ब्राजिलमा मात्र सीमित नहुने विश्लेषण अमेरिकी समाचार संस्था सीएनएनले गरेको छ । ल्याटिन अमेरिकाको सबैभन्दा ठूलो अर्थतन्त्र भएको ब्राजिलले लुलाको नेतृत्वमा तुलनात्मक रूपमा स्वतन्त्र विदेश नीति कायम राख्ने र अमेरिकाको अपेक्षा पूरा नहुने उल्लेख छ । लुलाले ब्राजिलको सार्वभौमिकतामा जोड दिँदै आएका छन्। साथै, अमेरिका र ब्राजिलबीच तनाव बढिरहेका बेला उनले ग्लोबल साउथका देशहरू तथा चीनसँग सम्बन्ध विस्तार गर्ने नीति अघि सारेका छन् । मतदान सकिनुअघि अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले ब्राजिलको दोस्रो चरणको निर्वाचनलाई आफूले निगरानी गरिरहेको बताएका थिए । उनले कुनै उम्मेदवारलाई समर्थन नगरे पनि यसअघि फ्लाभियो बोल्सोनारोको पहिलो चरणको प्रदर्शनको प्रशंसा गरेका थिए। उनले ब्राजिलको निर्वाचनलाई “अत्यन्त महत्त्वपूर्ण” पनि भनेका थिए । बोल्सोनारोले चुनावी नतिजालाई कानुनी चुनौती दिने घोषणा गरेसँगै ब्राजिलमा निर्वाचनपछिको राजनीतिक विवाद थप चर्किन सक्ने देखिएको छ । उनको यो घोषणालाई ट्रम्पले समर्थन गर्ने दाबी गरिएको छ । Kathmandu. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has been re-elected for a historic fourth term. However, his rival and ally of US President Donald Trump, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, has rejected the election results and said he will challenge them legally. Lula, an 80-year-old leftist leader, won the second round of the election with more than 51 percent of the vote. His victory is a relief for the left at a time when right-wing political trends are gaining strength in various Latin American countries. Bolsonaro, who trailed Lula by about 4.4 million votes, has questioned the results after the Supreme Court ruled to extend the voting period by two hours at the last minute. Addressing supporters in the capital Brasilia, he said: "Given the way events have unfolded, it is impossible to accept the election results. We will take legal action, we will demand the annulment of this election." The news reports state that this is the first time since direct presidential elections began in 1989 that a candidate who came in second in the first round has won the presidency after the second round of voting. American news organization CNN has analyzed that the impact of Lula's victory will not be limited to Brazil. It is noted that Brazil, the largest economy in Latin America, will maintain a relatively independent foreign policy under Lula's leadership and will not meet US expectations. Lula has emphasized Brazil's sovereignty. He has also pursued a policy of expanding relations with countries in the Global South and China, amid rising tensions between the United States and Brazil. Before the vote ended, US President Donald Trump said he was monitoring the second round of Brazil's election. Although he did not endorse any candidate, he had previously praised Flavio Bolsonaro's performance in the first round. He also called Brazil's election "extremely important." Bolsonaro's announcement that he will legally challenge the election results is likely to further intensify the post-election political conflict in Brazil. Trump is said to support his announcement.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has been re-elected for a historic fourth term. However, his rival and ally of US President Donald Trump, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, has rejected the election results and said he will challenge them legally. Lula, an 80-year-old leftist leader, won the second round of the election with more than 51 percent of the vote. His victory is a relief for the left at a time when right-wing political trends are gaining strength in various Latin American countries. Bolsonaro, who trailed Lula by about 4.4 million votes, has questioned the results after the Supreme Court ruled to extend the voting period by two hours at the last minute. Addressing supporters in the capital Brasilia, he said: "Given the way events have unfolded, it is impossible to accept the election results. We will take legal action, we will demand the annulment of this election." The news reports state that this is the first time since direct presidential elections began in 1989 that a candidate who came in second in the first round has won the presidency after the second round of voting. American news organization CNN has analyzed that the impact of Lula's victory will not be limited to Brazil. It is noted that Brazil, the largest economy in Latin America, will maintain a relatively independent foreign policy under Lula's leadership and will not meet US expectations. Lula has emphasized Brazil's sovereignty. He has also pursued a policy of expanding relations with countries in the Global South and China, amid rising tensions between the United States and Brazil. Before the vote ended, US President Donald Trump said he was monitoring the second round of Brazil's election. Although he did not endorse any candidate, he had previously praised Flavio Bolsonaro's performance in the first round. He also called Brazil's election "extremely important." Bolsonaro's announcement that he will legally challenge the election results is likely to further intensify the post-election political conflict in Brazil. Trump is said to support his announcement.

राजधानी ब्रासिलियामा समर्थकहरूलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै उनले भने–घटनाक्रम जसरी अघि बढ्यो, त्यसलाई हेर्दा चुनावी नतिजा स्वीकार गर्न असम्भव छ । हामी कानुनी कदम चाल्नेछौँ, यो चुनाव रद्द गर्न माग गर्नेछौँ।”

सन् १९८९ मा प्रत्यक्ष राष्ट्रपति निर्वाचनसुरु भएयता पहिलो चरणमा दोस्रो स्थानमा रहेका उम्मेदवारले दोस्रो चरणको मतदानपछि राष्ट्रपति पद जितेको यो पहिलो घटना भएको समाचारमा उल्लेख छ ।

लुलाको जितको प्रभाव ब्राजिलमा मात्र सीमित नहुने विश्लेषण अमेरिकी समाचार संस्था सीएनएनले गरेको छ ।

ल्याटिन अमेरिकाको सबैभन्दा ठूलो अर्थतन्त्र भएको ब्राजिलले लुलाको नेतृत्वमा तुलनात्मक रूपमा स्वतन्त्र विदेश नीति कायम राख्ने र अमेरिकाको अपेक्षा पूरा नहुने उल्लेख छ ।

लुलाले ब्राजिलको सार्वभौमिकतामा जोड दिँदै आएका छन्। साथै, अमेरिका र ब्राजिलबीच तनाव बढिरहेका बेला उनले ग्लोबल साउथका देशहरू तथा चीनसँग सम्बन्ध विस्तार गर्ने नीति अघि सारेका छन् ।

मतदान सकिनुअघि अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले ब्राजिलको दोस्रो चरणको निर्वाचनलाई आफूले निगरानी गरिरहेको बताएका थिए ।

उनले कुनै उम्मेदवारलाई समर्थन नगरे पनि यसअघि फ्लाभियो बोल्सोनारोको पहिलो चरणको प्रदर्शनको प्रशंसा गरेका थिए। उनले ब्राजिलको निर्वाचनलाई “अत्यन्त महत्त्वपूर्ण” पनि भनेका थिए ।

बोल्सोनारोले चुनावी नतिजालाई कानुनी चुनौती दिने घोषणा गरेसँगै ब्राजिलमा निर्वाचनपछिको राजनीतिक विवाद थप चर्किन सक्ने देखिएको छ । उनको यो घोषणालाई ट्रम्पले समर्थन गर्ने दाबी गरिएको छ ।

Kathmandu. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has been re-elected for a historic fourth term. However, his rival and ally of US President Donald Trump, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, has rejected the election results and said he will challenge them legally. Lula, an 80-year-old leftist leader, won the second round of the election with more than 51 percent of the vote. His victory is a relief for the left at a time when right-wing political trends are gaining strength in various Latin American countries. Bolsonaro, who trailed Lula by about 4.4 million votes, has questioned the results after the Supreme Court ruled to extend the voting period by two hours at the last minute. Addressing supporters in the capital Brasilia, he said: "Given the way events have unfolded, it is impossible to accept the election results. We will take legal action, we will demand the annulment of this election." The news reports state that this is the first time since direct presidential elections began in 1989 that a candidate who came in second in the first round has won the presidency after the second round of voting. American news organization CNN has analyzed that the impact of Lula's victory will not be limited to Brazil. It is noted that Brazil, the largest economy in Latin America, will maintain a relatively independent foreign policy under Lula's leadership and will not meet US expectations. Lula has emphasized Brazil's sovereignty. He has also pursued a policy of expanding relations with countries in the Global South and China, amid rising tensions between the United States and Brazil. Before the vote ended, US President Donald Trump said he was monitoring the second round of Brazil's election. Although he did not endorse any candidate, he had previously praised Flavio Bolsonaro's performance in the first round. He also called Brazil's election "extremely important." Bolsonaro's announcement that he will legally challenge the election results is likely to further intensify the post-election political conflict in Brazil. Trump is said to support his announcement.
